2 speaking attributes carry a string written inline: libs/components/widget/src/widget.ts: host `value` = "Delete the row" libs/components/widget/src/widget.ts: host `srcdoc` = "

Delete the row

"
description: Sentences a `host` block writes as the attributes an element of one tag draws: a field's `value` and an `<iframe>`'s `srcdoc`. The host's `type` decides nothing: the consumer's element writes its own over it (measured: `<input pctH type="text">` shows the value of a host writing `type: 'checkbox'`), and a host is any element. Point 2 compares neither, being no attribute that speaks on every element; so the refusal counts two.
